name: GPN
description: Masked DNA language model; variant effects scored by single-nucleotide masking.

attributes.source_locator: Tang et al. Table 1 and Methods

version.note: Family record; versions are on configurations

profile.summary: GPN (Genomic Pretrained Network, also called GPN-SS) is a DNA language model that learns from unaligned genome sequences alone. Given a 512-bp DNA window with some positions masked, it predicts the nucleotide at each masked position. Its main use is to score genetic variants without labels: the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The published model was trained on Arabidopsis thaliana and seven other Brassicales genomes.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md introduction; paper Fig. 1 caption; model card title

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN is a convolutional neural network, not a transformer. The masked DNA sequence is one-hot encoded with single nucleotides as tokens, then passed through 25 convolutional blocks. Each block has a dilated convolution and a feed-forward layer, with residual connections and layer normalisation; the embedding dimension stays at 512. Training is masked language modelling: 15% of positions are masked and predicted with a cross-entropy loss. To score a variant, only the variant position is masked, and the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The authors down-weighted repetitive elements in the loss; the card records a repeat weight of 0.1.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, Fig. 1 caption; model card: Some hparams

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The songlab-cal/gpn repository now covers four model families: GPN, GPN-MSA, PhyloGPN and GPN-Star. This page is about single-sequence GPN. Its published checkpoint is songlab/gpn-brassicales, which uses a seven-token DNA tokenizer. The same family also has an animal promoter model (songlab/gpn-animal-promoter) and a sorghum gene-expression model fine-tuned from gpn-brassicales. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read gpn-brassicales at revision eb9c35d0. The paper analyses are kept in an archive branch, and the maintained training recipe is in recipes/gpn_training. Note that the existing benchmark source (Tang et al. 2025) did not use gpn-brassicales: it evaluated a custom GPN pre-trained on the human reference genome.

strengths.text: Needs only a reference genome: the authors say the model can be applied to any species with one, without functional genomics data.
Single-nucleotide tokens make variant scoring direct: one position is masked and the two alleles compared.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods; Fig. 1 caption

strengths.text: Maintained package with a command-line tool for variant scoring, logits and embeddings, MIT licensed code and weights.

limitations.text: The published checkpoint is a plant model (Arabidopsis and seven other Brassicales). For other species, a user needs another checkpoint or must train one.
The context window is 512 bp, so it sees only local sequence around a variant.
The variant scorer accepts only biallelic SNVs, and the score is raw and uncalibrated.
The authors trained each model on GPUs (about 4 days on 4 NVIDIA A100 80 GB). The sources give no minimum hardware for inference; inference defaults to FP32 on any device.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods; docs/getting-started/cli.md: Devices and distributed execution

run_guide.summary: Install the gpn package with inference extras, load the published GPN checkpoint, and score SNVs from a table against a reference genome.
prerequisites: Python 3.13, which the package supports.
For CUDA, install PyTorch with the official PyTorch installer before or alongside GPN. The sources state no GPU type or memory for inference.
Your own inputs: a variants table (for example variants.parquet) of biallelic SNVs with one-based pos, and the matching reference genome FASTA. The published checkpoint is for Brassicales genomes.
Code and weights are MIT licensed. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell: pip install "gpn[inference]"
steps.explanation: Installs the gpn package with the file-backed inference commands. The PyPI release is not pinned to the commit read here.

steps.title: Load the published checkpoint
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

register_auto_classes("ss")

model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-brassicales")
PY
steps.explanation: The GPN quick-start snippet from the documentation, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the gpn-brassicales weights and loads them as a masked language model.

steps.title: Score variants
steps.shell:
gpn ss vep \
  --input-path variants.parquet \
  --genome-path genome.fa.gz \
  --window-size 512 \
  --model-path songlab/gpn-brassicales \
  --output-path scores.parquet \
  --per-device-eval-batch-size 64
steps.explanation: The documented variant scoring command. variants.parquet and genome.fa.gz are the user's own files; positions are one-based and the reference allele must match the genome.

outputs: scores.parquet, with one row per input variant. Its score column is the raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio averaged over both strands; negative values mean the alternate is less likely.
limitations: These commands were read from the documentation and have not been executed by Rewire.
pip installs the latest PyPI release, not the commit read here; the documentation pins Transformers exactly in the package metadata.
Inference defaults to FP32 without compilation; on GPU the documentation suggests adding --bf16-full-eval --torch-compile.

name: HyenaDNA
description: DNA language model pretrained on the human reference genome with context lengths of 32 kb to 1 Mb.

attributes.source_locator: Manzo et al. Table 2 and Table 3; Tang et al. Table 1 and Methods

version.note: Family record; versions are on configurations

profile.summary: HyenaDNA is a family of DNA language models that read very long stretches of genome one base at a time, up to 1 million bases in the largest model. It was pretrained on the human reference genome by predicting the next base, and it outputs per-base embeddings that can be fine-tuned for tasks such as finding regulatory elements or classifying species.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: Intro; model card: Model & Training Overview; arXiv abstract

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: HyenaDNA replaces attention with a stack of Hyena operators, which use input projections, implicit long convolutions and gating and scale sub-quadratically with sequence length. Each layer has a global receptive field. A single-character tokenizer with a vocabulary of the 4 nucleotides plus special tokens keeps single-base resolution. The model is causal: it is pretrained by next-nucleotide prediction on the human reference genome (HG38), and the inference script pads on the left for that reason.
sections.source_locator: model card: Model & Training Overview; huggingface.py: inference_single

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README lists seven pretrained checkpoints of different size and training sequence length, all trained on hg38: tiny-1k, tiny-1k-d256, tiny-16k-d128, small-32k, medium-160k, medium-450k and large-1m. Each exists as a weights-only repository for the original GitHub code and as a transformers-compatible copy with an -hf suffix; the model card says the two give identical outputs. A result should name the checkpoint, which interface was used, and the revision; this page read LongSafari/hyenadna-large-1m-seqlen-hf at revision 0a629abf. A Docker image with the exact Nucleotide Transformer benchmark settings from the paper is also provided.

strengths.text: Reads up to 1 million bases at single-base resolution in the largest checkpoint, without the k-mer or fixed tokenisers that the paper says lose single-nucleotide resolution.
Sizes run from tiny-1k to large-1m, and the developers give a suggested GPU for each: tiny-1k runs on a T4 for pretraining, fine-tuning and inference.
Weights are available both for the original training code and as transformers-compatible -hf copies with identical outputs, under permissive licences (BSD-3-Clause weights, Apache-2.0 code).

limitations.text: Pretrained only on the human reference genome hg38; no checkpoints trained on other species or on population variation are listed.
The model is causal and reads one direction. A bidirectional variant exists only for training from scratch on a downstream task, without masked language model pretraining.
Long contexts need large GPUs: the developers suggest an A100-40GB for inference with large-1m and A100-80GB for fine-tuning it.
The repository is described by its authors as a work in progress, and getting logits is not automated.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository's dependencies at a pinned commit and run the standalone huggingface.py script, which downloads a pretrained checkpoint and prints the shape of the embeddings for a sample sequence.
prerequisites: conda and git. The README asks for Python 3.8+ and says the repository is developed with Pytorch 1.13 and CUDA 11.7.
git lfs: huggingface.py downloads the checkpoint by running git lfs install and git clone.
A GPU is used when available, otherwise the script falls back to CPU. The developers suggest a T4 for inference up to medium-450k and an A100-40GB for large-1m.
Code is Apache-2.0 and weights BSD-3-Clause. The weights are not gated.

profile.summary: CI-SpliceAI predicts whether a DNA variant disrupts RNA splicing. It keeps the SpliceAI deep convolutional network design but retrains it on manually curated GENCODE splice sites, with all isoforms of a gene collapsed into one, and on all chromosomes. Given a VCF file and a human reference genome, it reports for each variant the predicted gain or loss of acceptor and donor sites and where they occur.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract, Introduction; README: Differences to SpliceAI, Output

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: CI-SpliceAI uses the SpliceAI design: five deep convolutional neural networks that label every nucleotide as acceptor, donor or neither, using 10,000 nucleotides of flanking context. For training, GENCODE v37 (GRCh38) transcripts with automated (level 3) annotation were removed, and all remaining splice sites of a gene were merged into one collapsed isoform. Sequences were cut into 15,000-base windows, each predicting 5,000 central nucleotides. The training procedure was reimplemented from SpliceAI, with categorical cross-entropy and the Adam optimiser. The five trained networks are packed into one frozen graph. To score a variant, the tool predicts on the reference and the variant sequence and reports the change (delta score) for acceptor and donor gain and loss.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Introduction; Methods, Splice site recognition; Algorithmic comparison on variant data; Train README: aggregate.py

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper trained the model twice: on SpliceAI's 19 training chromosomes, for a fair comparison, and on all chromosomes, which is the final model shipped in the annotation package as the frozen file CI-SpliceAI.pb. steps.title: Predict splice site probabilities for custom sequences
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from cispliceai.model import CISpliceAI
from cispliceai.data import DNAPreprocessor

model = CISpliceAI()

# you can run multiple sequences in a batch
# you can input sequences of varying length, but it's your responsibility to ensure that the batch fits on memory!
# The sequences here are only an example, you should upload much longer slices to get sensible results
predictions = model.predict([
  DNAPreprocessor.onehot_and_pad('CTTCCTCTCCTCCTGCCCCACCTTCCTCTCCTCCTGCCCCACCAGAACCGGGGGCGGCTGGCAGACAAGAGGACAGTCGCCCTGCCTGCC'),
  DNAPreprocessor.onehot_and_pad('CTCCTCCTGCCCCACCAGAACCGGGGGCGGCTG'),
])

# Get acceptor and donor scores for the two sequences
acceptor_prob_1 = predictions[0][:, 1]
donor_prob_1 = predictions[0][:, 2]

acceptor_prob_2 = predictions[1][:, 1]
donor_prob_2 = predictions[1][:, 2]
PY
steps.explanation: The README's custom-sequence example (available since version 1.1), wrapped in a shell heredoc. It loads the bundled model and computes per-nucleotide acceptor and donor probabilities for two short example sequences.

profile.summary: SpliceAI2 is a deep learning model from Illumina that predicts RNA splicing from genomic sequence. It reads about 200 kb of DNA around a gene and predicts how much each position is used as a splice donor or acceptor, how much each splice junction is used, and the most likely complete transcripts. Comparing predictions for reference and alternate alleles gives a score for how strongly a variant changes splicing.
profile.summary_source_locator: Manuscript: Main 'Hierarchical model of RNA splicing'; Methods 'Variant effect prediction'; README: introduction

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The input is 196,608 bp of genomic sequence on the gene's sense strand, one-hot encoded, plus a one-hot code for the species (ten channels). A dense layer projects it to 256 channels, and 20 MetaFormer blocks follow, each with a depth-wise dilated convolution and a feed-forward network, at progressively coarser pooling. Each block's output feeds a splice site head over the central 65,536 positions. The 1,024 positions with the highest splice site usage are then paired by a query-key product to give a 1,024 by 1,024 matrix of splice junction usage. Sites and junctions form a splice graph, and Viterbi decoding finds the highest scoring paths, which are the predicted transcripts. The model was trained end-to-end on splice site, junction and transcript usage, with the three losses summed.
sections.source_locator: Manuscript: Methods 'SpliceAI2 model' (Inputs, Architecture, Outputs, Training); 'Transcript prediction'

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The code is package version 2.0 (this page read commit 1dcd2a18 on main). The released model is an ensemble of two checkpoints trained with identical settings, held on Hugging Face as spliceai2_multispecies_13M_01 and spliceai2_multispecies_13M_02, each with a model.ckpt; the README's commands pass both folders. Illumina also publishes precomputed scores for all possible single nucleotide variants and observed indels in protein-coding genes (GENCODE v48, GRCh38). The manuscript also describes a tissue-specific model conditioned on RBP expression; the files read do not show it as released. A result should name the package version, both checkpoint folders and the Hugging Face revision (55948bae read here).

strengths.text: It predicts splice junctions and whole transcripts as well as splice sites, so a variant's effect can be read as a change in transcript structure, not only a site score.
Long context: each prediction sees 196,608 bp of sequence.
Precomputed scores cover all possible single nucleotide variants and observed indels in human protein-coding genes, and the output keeps SpliceAI-compatible columns and threshold equivalents.
The authors report improved detection of splice-altering variants and better quantification of their effects across cryptic splicing, sQTL and MPRA benchmarks; this is their claim.

A CUDA-capable GPU is required.
Weights are gated on Hugging Face and need a manual access request with academic details.
The user must supply the gene strand for each variant; if it is unknown, both strands have to be scored and combined.

profile.summary: GPN-Promoter (Hugging Face name gpn-animal-promoter) is a DNA language model trained on promoter sequences from animal genomes. It was released with TraitGym, a benchmark of causal regulatory variants in human genetics. Given a DNA window, it predicts masked nucleotides; the GPN tools turn this into a variant score, the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele, or into sequence embeddings.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md: Animal promoter model and TraitGym; TraitGym README: Code; model card: Basic usage; docs/getting-started/cli.md: GPN

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN-Promoter belongs to the GPN (GPN-SS) family: single-sequence genomic language models trained on unaligned genomes with masked language modelling. The published config uses the GPN model type with a ByteNet-style convolutional encoder of 64 layers and hidden size 1024, a first kernel size of 9 and later kernel size of 5, with dilation base 2 cycling every 8 layers. The vocabulary has 7 tokens, from the tokenizer gonzalobenegas/tokenizer-dna-mlm named in the training script. The archived training command used a dataset version called v6/512, 64 layers and hidden size 1024, with a total batch size of 2048. For variant scoring, the GPN package compares the model's likelihood of the alternate and reference alleles, averaged over both strands.
sections.source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md; config.json; archived train.sh and README.md; docs/getting-started/cli.md

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility

Intermediate training checkpoints from the same run are in a separate Hugging Face dataset, and the training data are in songlab/gpn-animal-promoter-dataset. The analysis code that produced the model is preserved under the ref analysis-archive-2026-08-18 of the GPN repository. The model card imports gpn.model, while the current GPN docs (commit dc5fd287 read here) load GPN models through register_auto_classes("ss"). profile.summary: FramePool predicts how strongly a 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) drives translation, measured as mean ribosome load, directly from the 5' UTR sequence. It is a convolutional network trained on a massively parallel reporter assay, made to accept 5' UTRs of any length by pooling motif detections separately in each of the three reading frames. Through Kipoi, it takes variants from a VCF file and reports the predicted log2 fold change in mean ribosome load for each affected 5' UTR.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; README; Kipoi model.yaml: info.doc

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: FramePool adapts the published MPRA model of Sample et al. That model used a dense layer, so it only worked for the sequence lengths it was trained on. FramePool keeps three convolutional layers (kernel size 7, 128 filters each, with residual skip connections) and replaces the position-specific dense input with global max and average pooling, done separately for each of the three frames relative to the start codon. The pooled values (a vector of 768) go into a dense layer of 64 neurons and a final linear output. Each model has 282,625 learnable weights; the combined model has 4 more in a scaling layer. The model was trained with the Adam optimiser and a mean squared error loss.
sections.source_locator: README; Paper: Methods, Framepool model; Model training

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper trains three models: FramePool50 on 50-nucleotide MPRA sequences, FramePool100 on 25 to 100 nucleotide sequences, and FramePoolCombined on both, with a scaling layer for the two libraries. The paper names FramePoolCombined as the model for variant effect prediction from VCF files. The Kipoi zoo entry downloads the weights file Framepool_combined_residual.h5 from Zenodo record 3584238 with a fixed md5 checksum. A result should name the Kipoi model (Framepool), the weights checksum and the kipoi/models commit; this page read commit 770dcaf2.

strengths.text: Small model: 282,625 learnable weights. On the 20,000 held-out 50-nucleotide MPRA sequences, the authors report a Pearson correlation of 0.964 for FramePool50 against 0.966 for Optimus50.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Methods; Results, Evaluating frame pooling on MPRA data

limitations.text: Cannot reliably detect upstream open reading frames longer than 19 nucleotides, and cannot model the order of upstream start sites, so leaky scanning is only partly captured.
Trained on reporter assay data from one cell line (HEK293T, eGFP library), so it predicts the effect of 5' UTR sequence only, without coding sequence or 3' UTR context.
The Kipoi environment pins an old stack: Python 3.7, TensorFlow 1.13.1, Keras 2.2.4 and h5py 2.9.0.

Variant scoring through Kipoi expects a single-sample VCF: the BED and VCF must be sorted with a tabix index, chromosome naming must match across files, and a VCF that mixes patients gives results that are not meaningful.

run_guide.summary: Install Kipoi, create the Framepool environment, and score the example variants with the Kipoi command line, as shown on the Kipoi model page.
prerequisites: conda (anaconda or miniconda), which Kipoi uses to manage model dependencies. Kipoi maintains Python 3.6 to 3.10.
For Python 3.8 to 3.10, the Kipoi README says hdf5 and pkgconfig must be installed before Kipoi.
The Framepool environment itself pins Python 3.7, TensorFlow 1.13.1 and Keras 2.2.4. A GPU is not mentioned.
Code and weights are MIT licensed.

steps.title: Install Kipoi
steps.shell: pip install kipoi
steps.explanation: The Kipoi README install command. It installs the latest Kipoi release, not a pinned version.

steps.title: Create and activate the Framepool environment
steps.shell:
kipoi env create Framepool
source activate kipoi-Framepool
steps.explanation: Creates a conda environment with the dependencies from the Framepool model definition and activates it.
steps.source_locator: Kipoi page: CLI, Create a new conda environment

steps.title: Score the example variants
steps.shell:
kipoi get-example Framepool -o example
kipoi predict Framepool \
  --dataloader_args='{"intervals_file": "example/intervals_file", "fasta_file": "example/fasta_file", "vcf_file": "example/vcf_file", "vcf_file_tbi": "example/vcf_file_tbi", "chr_order_file": "example/chr_order_file", "num_chr": true}' \
  -o '/tmp/Framepool.example_pred.tsv'
# check the results
head '/tmp/Framepool.example_pred.tsv'
steps.explanation: The Kipoi page's prediction commands, with HTML entities decoded. They download the example BED, FASTA and VCF files, run the model on them and show the first lines of the output table.
steps.source_locator: Kipoi page: CLI, Make a prediction

outputs: A tab-separated file, /tmp/Framepool.example_pred.tsv, with predicted log2 fold changes in mean ribosome load (mrl_fold_change, shift_1, shift_2) per variant and 5' UTR, of which head prints the first lines.
limitations: These commands were read from the Kipoi page and README and have not been executed by Rewire.
The Kipoi README notes h5py compatibility issues for models saved with h5py below version 3; the Framepool environment pins h5py 2.9.0.
To retrain or reproduce the paper, the README points to the Model_Training.ipynb notebook and the Zenodo data instead; that route is not covered here.

profile.summary: GPN-Star is a DNA language model that predicts how strongly each position of a genome is constrained by evolution, and so how damaging a single-nucleotide variant there is likely to be. It reads a window of a whole-genome alignment of many species with their species tree, predicts masked nucleotides of the target genome, and scores a variant by how much less likely the alternate allele is than the reference. Human models exist at vertebrate, mammal and primate timescales, and further models cover five model organisms.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract and Main; docs/models/gpn-star.md: opening paragraph and Models; cli.md: GPN section on the output score

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN-Star is an encoder-only Transformer trained to predict masked nucleotides. Each input is a window of a whole-genome alignment and its species tree. The alignment is split into target sequences and source sequences. Source species that are closely related are pooled into clade-level representations. Each encoder block has self-attention along the target sequence, a phylogeny-informed cross-attention module that reads the source sequences weighted by evolutionary distances from the species tree, and a feed-forward network. The published vertebrate human checkpoint has 16 layers, hidden size 1024 and 16 attention heads.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Main, Fig. 1 legend and model description; config.json

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Eight checkpoints are published. Three are human (hg38) models of 200M parameters each, trained on a 100-way vertebrate, a 447-way mammalian and a 243-way primate alignment; the paper calls them GPN-Star (V), (M) and (P). Five are for model organisms: mouse and chicken (85M parameters), fly (85M), worm and arabidopsis (25M). Each checkpoint needs the alignment it was trained on, with matching assembly, species set, species order and evolutionary scale. Genome-wide scores are published, so many uses need no inference. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision, whether published scores or new inference were used, and the window size.

facts.value: Phylogeny-aware masked DNA language model over whole-genome alignments

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Encoder-only Transformer (GPNStarForMaskedLM) with sequence-wise self-attention and phylogeny-informed cross-attention to clade-level source embeddings. The vertebrate human checkpoint: 16 layers, hidden size 1024, 16 attention heads, intermediate size 4096.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Main; config.json

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A window of a prepared whole-genome alignment with its species tree, read from a local Zarr store that matches the checkpoint. Variant scoring takes biallelic single-nucleotide variants with one-based positions and an even window size.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Main; cli.md: GPN and GPN-Star sections

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A raw, uncalibrated log-likelihood ratio per variant; masked-nucleotide logits; or embeddings. The paper's analyses use scores calibrated for mutation rate, which is a separate step.
facts.source_locator: cli.md: GPN-Star; paper: Main

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Human checkpoints (v100, m447, p243): 200M each; the safetensors file of gpn-star-hg38-v100-200m holds 203,022,198. Mouse, chicken and fly: 85M each. Worm and arabidopsis: 25M each.

strengths.text: Genome-wide scores are published for the human genome and the five model organisms, so variants can be looked up without running the model.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Data availability; docs/models/gpn-star.md: Alignments and scores

strengths.text: Training cost is modest by the authors' account: the 200 million parameter models were trained for several days on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

Separate human models at three evolutionary timescales let a user choose; the authors report that deeper timescales better capture coding and highly constrained regions, and shallower ones better inform fast-evolving regulatory elements.
Code and weights are MIT licensed, and the package supports both inference and training on prepared alignments.
strengths.source_locator: README.md; Hugging Face API response; docs/models/gpn-star.md: opening paragraph

limitations.text: Inference needs a whole-genome alignment that matches the checkpoint. The human vertebrate archive is about 42 GB compressed, more once extracted, and the command-line tool does not download it.
Variant scoring covers biallelic single-nucleotide variants. The authors say the fixed alignment format makes the model less suited to indels and structural variants.
Scores from the command-line tool are raw and uncalibrated. The paper's results use mutation-rate calibrated scores, so raw output is not directly comparable to them.
The model is trained on DNA sequence alone and is not specific to any tissue.

run_guide.summary: Install the gpn package, load the vertebrate human checkpoint, download and arrange its alignment, and score variants from the command line.
prerequisites: For many uses no run is needed: genome-wide scores are published at https://huggingface.co/datasets/songlab/gpn-star-scores.
Python with pip. The repository badge names Python 3.13.
Disk space for the vertebrate alignment archive: about 42 GB compressed, plus more for the extracted Zarr store. The hf, sha256sum and unpigz commands are used to fetch and unpack it.

Variants as biallelic single-nucleotide variants with one-based positions. The GPN-Star section of the command-line guide does not list accepted file formats; the GPN-MSA section lists Parquet, CSV/TSV, VCF, GTF and GFF.
GPU need is not stated; inference defaults to FP32 on any device.

steps.title: Install the package with inference dependencies
steps.shell: pip install "gpn[inference]"
steps.explanation: The inference extra is required for the file-backed commands.

steps.title: Load the checkpoint in Python
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

register_auto_classes("star")
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-star-hg38-v100-200m")
PY
steps.explanation: The documentation's quick start, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the weights from Hugging Face.

steps.title: Download and verify the vertebrate alignment
steps.shell:
hf download songlab/multiz100way-pigz 99.zarr.tar.gz \
  --repo-type dataset \
  --revision 6a9d42a35e7debbba845979dea6064f14d5cb3f9 \
  --local-dir .

echo '4dad7da04db9c804032c0c4c7bbefea58f694fc911e962d28c8df87f356ce4ad  99.zarr.tar.gz' \
  | sha256sum --check
unpigz --stdout 99.zarr.tar.gz | tar -xf -
steps.explanation: Copied from the documentation. The archive extracts as 99.zarr.

steps.title: Arrange the alignment store
steps.shell:
mkdir -p /path/to/multiz100way/100
mv 99.zarr /path/to/multiz100way/100/all.zarr
steps.explanation: These two lines are written by Rewire from the documentation's prose, which asks for the extracted store to be moved or symlinked to /path/to/multiz100way/100/all.zarr; the directory name 100 is significant. Replace /path/to with a real location.

steps.title: Score variants
steps.shell:
gpn star vep \
  --input-path INPUT_PATH \
  --msa-path /path/to/multiz100way \
  --window-size WINDOW_SIZE \
  --model-path songlab/gpn-star-hg38-v100-200m \
  --output-path OUTPUT_PATH
steps.explanation: The command template from the command-line guide, with the alignment path and the model name from the documentation filled in by Rewire. Replace INPUT_PATH with a variant file, WINDOW_SIZE with an even number and OUTPUT_PATH with a Parquet file name. The sources read do not give the window size for this checkpoint. Chromosome names must match the store, and the reference allele must match the alignment or inference stops.
steps.source_locator: cli.md: GPN-Star; docs/models/gpn-star.md: Inspect a local interval

outputs: A Parquet file at OUTPUT_PATH with one row per input variant and a score column: the raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio. Negative values mean the alternate allele is less likely than the reference.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The window size for the published checkpoints is not given in the sources read, and scores depend on it.
Other checkpoints need their own matching alignment; only the vertebrate human alignment has download steps in the documentation read.
